question: Will the White House have a named permanent press secretary succeeding Katie Zacharia as of October 30, 2026?

calls.reasoning: As of Oct 19 2026 the press secretary post is vacant: no successor and no acting press secretary named. Wikipedia lists it as vacant since Oct 16. NBC, citing two people familiar with Trump's thinking, reported a new press secretary is unlikely to be named soon. The previous search (Leavitt's exit to Zacharia's naming) took about 6 weeks, and Zacharia's collapse argues for slower vetting. Against that, Trump announces picks quickly on social media and has a ready insider (deputy Anna Kelly) and an eager outsider (Jennings). Polymarket's 'announced by Oct 31' contract, a near match ending one day later and not excluding acting picks, traded around 15% per the harness candidate list (~$216k volume); I did not confirm that price myself. I land slightly below it.
calls.dossier:
- Katie Zacharia was named press secretary by Trump on Oct 9 2026 (CNN, CNBC), gave her first briefing Oct 13, and was out Oct 16 after 5 days (CNBC, Al Jazeera, Oct 16). The bar-exam/lawyer misrepresentation was central.
- Wikipedia's White House Press Secretary page (checked Oct 19) lists the office as 'Vacant since October 16, 2026'. No acting press secretary is mentioned.
- NBC News (via Sentinel Assam, Oct 18), citing two people familiar with Trump's thinking: a new press secretary is unlikely to be appointed soon. A senior official said Zacharia would move to a new role to be announced later.
- Names in circulation (Daily Beast/HollywoodLife/Unilad, Oct 17-19): principal deputy Anna Kelly (early Kalshi favorite on Oct 16), Scott Jennings (overtook Kelly on Kalshi; publicly pitching himself), Margo Martin (floated by Trump to reporters), and Steven Cheung (mentioned). George Santos pitched himself (The Hill).
- Previous search: Leavitt left late August 2026 and Zacharia was named Oct 9, about 6 weeks. CNN reported candidates were disqualified over past criticism of Trump. In Aug 2026 Kalshi traders gave only 40% to an announcement within about 2 weeks (Kalshi news, Aug 23), and it in fact took about 6 weeks.
- Historical Trump vacancies: Sanders' departure was announced Jun 13 2019 and Grisham named Jun 25 2019 (~12 days). Grisham->McEnany was a same-day swap in Apr 2020. Spicer resigned Jul 21 2017 and Sanders was named the same day.
- Trump typically announces picks on Truth Social/X.
- Status quo: the post stays vacant, with deputies handling briefings.
- Resolves off a public announcement by the President or White House naming a permanent press secretary; acting/interim designations do not count. Checkable via the Wikipedia incumbent field.
- Event window: Oct 16 2026 -> Oct 30 2026 23:59 ET. As of Oct 19 11:40 UTC, about 21% of the window has elapsed (~11.5 days remain).
- Searched for any successor announcement on Oct 18-19: none found. Also searched for an acting designation: none found.

Shading slightly below the market because an acting/deputy designation does not count here.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs converge at 0.12-0.13 on identical evidence: vacant post, NBC 'unlikely soon', Trump 'no rush', 6-week prior search, Polymarket Oct 31 ~15c. The only factual uncertainty is whether the Polymarket contract counts acting designations, which I cannot settle without web access. Either way that clause plus the extra day makes the market a slight upper bound for this question. The judgment on how impulsive Trump will be is shared by all runs. I take 0.12, consistent with the market minus its looser terms.
